recipe_change: Keep GRB_CB_MIPNODE, status == GRB_OPTIMAL (status 1 fires too), MIPNODE_REL, GRBcbcut. Changes: (1) Fold duplicates is mandatory, not hygiene: past NumVars entries GRBcbcut corrupts the heap with return 0. The future add_user_cut(distinct_variables, ...) would reach that overflow under NDEBUG, where _check_distinct compiles out: maintainer's call whether to add a size check there. (2) Strip zeros, skip empty and drop satisfied have no effect on Gurobi, keep them only for backend uniformity. (3) Set PreCrush=1 only while a node callback is set, and document its cost (see measurements); the maintainer rules on restore. (4) Size the REL buffer from NumVars without calling update, and read Obj once per solve: value is exact, the read is O(n). (5) Contract text verbatim: 'valid for every integer feasible point'; dominance cuts give wrong status under PreCrush=1.

shipped_code_findings: include/mippp/solvers/gurobi/impl/v1/gurobi_milp.hpp:230 set_candidate_solution_callback neither resets the model nor invalidates results, so a callback set after a finished solve is never called by the next solve(), which returns the old answer as optimal. Reproduction: verify_gurobi_shipped lazyafter, degree-only TSP n=30: 'after_finish: first optimal 345 | then optimal value=345 callback calls=0 lazy added=0 cycles in the returned point=13 NOT A TOUR'; seed 2 also 397, 11 cycles. Controls: 'before' gives 476, a tour; 'after_change' (an Obj write) gives 476, a tour. After a solution-limit stop the resumed search does call it and returned a tour on both seeds. Docs do not warn; I did not check other backends. Maintainer decides between GRBreset on attach after a solve and a doc note.

Not a defect, checked: add_lazy_constraint(distinct_variables, ...) with a repeated variable aborts on the debug assert in model_base.hpp:314, and under -DNDEBUG GRBcblazy from MIPSOL is clean (valgrind 0 errors at x10). The heap overflow is GRBcbcut and cblazy at MIPNODE, so it concerns the future handle, not shipped code.
recommendation: Ship the recipe, with the changes in recipe_change. G1 stands: there is no local cut on Gurobi, so 'valid for every integer feasible point' is the only sound contract, and I could not break it with a valid cut. Three things must reach the maintainer: fold is safety, not hygiene; PreCrush=1 costs 100 to 300 times the nodes on models with parallel integer or binary columns, so set it only with a node callback and document it; a callback set after a finished solve is silently never called. Suite cases with power: X1 (fold), C5 and C10 (tree), C1 n=44 seed 9, C8 at stop 44 and first 0.3 s, G1's own subtree-cut instance. C4 needs euclidean distances to have any power; a point_ok check is needed for the filter; PreCrush can only be tested by enforcement counters.
